answer_1.quote: We demonstrate that LLMs, when finetuned on this dataset, can generate more grounded narrative text compared to language models tuned without game state information.
answer_1.outputs: The paper focuses on two main NLG-related tasks: (1) Utterance to Command — predicting a game command from natural language utterances, and (2) State to Narration — generating a narrative description of the effects of a game action based on state changes.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the generated commands over four quantitative metrics: pass rate, unit tests, RougeL and Average Sentence Gleu (SGleu).

answer_4.quote: We also perform a human evaluation to assess the quality of the generated utterances. In total, we recruited 45 evaluators from the Avrae user base based on their experience with Avrae and D&D.
answer_4.guideline: The evaluators were asked to rate each output along three dimensions: (1) Does the response make sense? (yes/no), (2) Is the response specific? (yes/no), (3) How interesting is the response? (10 point scale).
